223.subject: Botany
223.text: Assertion : In tropical rain forests, O-horizon and A-horizon of soil profile are shallow and nutrient-poor. Reason : Excessive growth of micro-organisms in the soil depletes its organic content.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of the assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of the assertion
If assertion is true, but reason is false
Both assertion and reason are false statements.
223.sol: A cross section of well developed soil shows more or less distinct layers called horizons. Ohorizon is the topmost layer of soil and A-horizon comes below O horizon. In the topmost layer, vegetation grows and various biological activities takes place. Tropical rain forests are found in tropical zone of the world and are characterized by very high temperature and abundance of rainfall. Soil in these area are red latosols and are exceedingly thick. Leaching of minerals from the top soil occurs rapidly but cycling of

303.subject: Botany
303.text: Assertion : Photomodulation of flowering is a phytochrome - regulated process. Reason : Active form of phytochrome (Pfr) directly induces floral induction in shoot buds.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false.
303.sol: Flowering is a phytochrome regulated process. Phytotchrome is a blue protein pigment with a molecular mass of about 125 k Da (kilodaltons). Phytochrome occurs in two interconvertible form P_R (which absorbs red light) and P _ fr (which absorbs far red light). The studies with mutants of Arabidopsis support and prove that the P _ fr is the active form of phytochrome. When P _ R molecules are exposed to red light, most of them absorb it and converted to P _ fr . This causes floral induction in the shoot.

options: aligned & 5^ -C G A A T G-3^ & 3^ -C G A A T G-5^ aligned
1898.sol: The palindromes in DNA are base pair sequences that are the same when read forward (left to right) or backward (right to left) from a central axis of symmetry. The following sequence reads the same on the two strands in 5^ 3^ direction. This is also true when we read in the 3^ 5^ direction. 1936.sol: Within the myocardium of the ventricles of heart, the branches of bundle of His (mass of specialised fibres) divide into a network of fine fibres called Purkinje fibres. The bundle of His and the Purkinje fibres convey impulse of contraction from AV node to the myocardium of ventricles.

1952.subject: Zoology
1952.text: The crystal of lead zirconate is a key component of
1952.sol: Sonography is a technique to visualise the structures beneath the skin. A transducer is used to recieve soundwave and signals to the skin. The transducer contains the crystals of lead zirconate that convert electric current into sound waves. Transducer also act as a reciever and converts the echoes into electrical signals which are processed and displayed on the screen of a monitor to show 2-D image.

2199.subject: Zoology
2199.text: Assertion : Corpus callosum connects the two cerebral hemispheres. Reason : Association areas are responsible for complex functions like intersensory association of memory and communication.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false

2199.sol: The cerebrum is the largest and most complex of all the parts of the human brain. It consists of left and right hemispheres connected by a large bundle of myelinated fibres, the corpus callosum. Association areas interpret the input, store the input and initiate a response in light of similar past experience. Thus, the association areas are involved in memory, learning and reasoning.

58724.subject: Chemistry
58724.text: Which alkaline earth metal carbonate decomposes most easily?
58724.sol: The thermal stability of alkaline earth metal carbonates increases down the group from Be to Ba . This is because as the size of the cation increases, its polarizing power decreases. A smaller cation like Mg²⁺ polarizes the large carbonate ion ( CO₃²⁻ ) more effectively, weakening the C-O bond and facilitating its decomposition into the metal oxide and CO₂ . The order of thermal stability is MgCO₃ Therefore, MgCO₃ has the lowest thermal stability among the given options and decomposes most easily. Answer: MgCO ₃

121278.sol: These bacteria are special since they live in some of the most harsh habitatssuch as extreme salty areas (halophiles), hot springs (thermoacidophiles)and marshy areas (methanogens). 121292.subject: Botany
121292.text: What material are the cell walls of diatoms made of?
121292.sol: This group includes diatoms and golden algae (desmids). They are found in fresh water as well as in marine environments. They are microscopic and float passively in water currents (plankton). Most of them are photosynthetic. In diatoms the cell walls form two thin overlapping shells, which fit together as in a soap box. The walls are embedded with silica and thus the walls are indestructible. Thus, diatoms have left behind large amount of cell wall deposits in their habitat; this accumulation over billions of years

The spores of slime molds lack cell walls How many of the above statements are correct?
122058.sol: The spore of Equisetum germinate shortly after shedding and gives rise to form prothallus. Prothalli of Equisetum are basically monoecious and the gametophytes are rarely seen. The simplest known sporophyte among bryophytes is that of Riccia while highest evolved known is Bryopsida (Polytrichum, Pogonatum). Sexual reproduction in Volvox is oogamous type. The spores in slime molds (e.g., Physarum) are haploid, unicellular, usually globose with smooth, spiny or reticulately thickened cell walls.

122150.subject: Botany
122150.text: Which of the following is not the feature of gymnosperms?
122150.sol: Gymnosperms (Gymno = naked; sperma = seed) are naked seed bearing perennial plants. In gymnosperms, there is no fruit formation (because ovary is absent); xylem without vessels and phloem without companion cells and have distinct branches.

122733.subject: Botany
122733.text: What are the four different kinds of whorls in a typical flower?
122733.sol: The flower is the reproductive unit in the angiosperms. It is meant for sexual reproduction. A typical flower has four different kinds of whorls arranged successively on the swollen end of the stalk or pedicel, called thalamus or receptacle. These are calyx, corolla, androecium and gynoecium. Calyx and corolla are accessory organs, while androecium and gynoecium are reproductive organs.

122888.sol: A leaf is said to be simple, when its lamina is entire or when incised, the incisions do not touch the midrib. When the incisions, of the lamina reach up to the midrib breaking it into a number of leaflets, the leaf is called compound. A bud is present in the axil of petiole in both simple and compound leaves, but not in the axil of leaflets of the compound leaf.

123554.subject: Botany

123554.sol: The M Phase starts with the nuclear division, corresponding to the separation of daughter chromosomes (karyokinesis) and usually ends with division of cytoplasm (cytokinesis). The interphase, though called the resting phase, is the time during which the cell is preparing for division by undergoing both cell growth and DNA replication in an orderly manner. The interphase is divided into three further phases: G₁ phase (Gap 1), S phase (Synthesis) and G₂ phase (Gap 2)

126425.sol: Reproduction without actual fertilisation is called as parthenogenesis. It is a type of reproduction in which formation of an embryo from an unfertilised egg takes place. Parthenocarpy is the process of production of fruit without fertilisation (pollination).

At the left extreme, the enzyme is preserved in a temporarily inactive state, whereas at the right extreme, it

At the left extreme of the curve (very low temperatures), the enzyme is preserved in a temporarily inactive state, meaning its structure is intact but it lacks the thermal energy required for catalysis. 128031.subject: Zoology
128031.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: The colour of dorsal skin of the frog is uniformly pale yellow while the ventral side is generally olive green with dark irregular spots. Reason: The frog drinks water but never absorbs through the skin.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
128031.sol: The colour of dorsal side of body is generally olive green with dark irregular spots. On the ventral side the skin is uniformly pale yellow. The frog never drinks water but absorb it through the skin.

128625.subject: Zoology
128625.text: Assertion : Insulin forms hormone receptor complex which regulates the formation of second messenger. Reason : Insulin is a peptide hormone which can easily pass through cell membrane to interact with intracellular receptors in cell cytoplasm.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
128625.sol: Insulin is a peptide hormone produced in the islets of Langerhans in the pancreas. Insulin interacts with membrane bound receptors and does not enter target cell but generates second messenger. Insulin receptors for most cells are less than 100 . Insulin binds to receptors located on plasma membrane to form hormone receptor complex which induces release of GDP from G protein which activates adenyl cyclase that in turn catalysis the formation of cyclic adenosine monophosphate (cAMP) from ATP. The hormone is called f

128629.subject: Zoology
128629.text: Assertion : Pituitary is attached to hypothalamus by a vein. Reason : This attachment is done through a hypophysial portal vein.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
128629.sol: Pituitary gland or hypophysis is situated in a depression, the sella turcica of sphenoid bone of the skull. It is directly attached to the hypothalamus by a stalk, the infundibulum. Hypophysial portal veins carry blood containing neurohormones (releasing factors) from the hypothalamus to the anterior pituitary.

128759.subject: Zoology
128759.text: Which of the following represents the dental formula of man?
128759.sol: The number and kinds of teeth in a species of mammals can be represented by a sort of equation, which is called dental formula. The dental formula of man is 2 1 2 3 2 1 2 3 =32 .

128788.subject: Zoology
128788.text: What is the shape of RBCs?
128788.sol: Erythrocytes or red blood cells (RBC) are the most abundant of all the cells in blood. A healthy adult man has, on an average, 5 million to 5.5 million of RBCs mm–3 of blood. RBCs are formed in the red bone marrow in the adults. RBCs are devoid of nucleus in most of the mammals and are biconcave in shape . They have a red colored, iron containing complex protein called haemoglobin, hence the color and name of these cells. A healthy individual has 12-16 gms of haemoglobin in every 100 ml of blood. 128880.subject: Zoology
128880.text: What happens to the atria during ventricular systole?
128880.sol: The SAN now generates an action potential which stimulates both the atria to undergo a simultaneous contraction – the atrial systole. This increases the flow of blood into the ventricles by about 30 per cent. The action potential is conducted to the ventricular side by the AVN and AV bundle from where the bundle of His transmits it through the entire ventricular musculature. This causes the ventricular muscles to contract, (ventricular systole), the atria undergoes relaxation (diastole) , coinciding with the ventri

options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
128968.sol: Fibrinogens are needed for clotting or coagulation of blood. Globulins primarily are involved in defense mechanisms of the body.

129084.subject: Zoology
129084.text: Which of the following statements are correct regarding monocytes? A. They are the most abundant white blood cells. B. They are classified as agranulocytes. C. They possess a kidney-shaped nucleus. D. They secrete histamine and serotonin. E. They are phagocytic cells that destroy foreign organisms. Choose the correct answer from the options below:
129084.sol: Leucocytes are divided into granulocytes (neutrophils, eosinophils, and basophils) and agranulocytes (lymphocytes and monocytes). Thus, monocytes are agranulocytes (Statement B is correct). Neutrophils are the most abundant WBCs (60-65%), whereas monocytes comprise 6-8% of total WBCs (Statement A is incorrect). According to NCERT diagrams, monocytes have a kidney-shaped nucleus (Statement C is correct). Basophils secrete histamine, serotonin, and heparin, not monocytes (Statement D is incorrect). Neutrophils and mo

129385.subject: Zoology
129385.text: Which of the following is true for the function of labelled parts in the diagram below?
options: A - Blind spot - Image is formed here
B - Fovea - No visual activity is present
C - Cornea - Helps to hold lens in place
D - Iris – Visible coloured portion of eye
129385.sol: A - Fovea centralis : Sharpest vision occurs here. B - Blindspot : No image is formed here. C - Ciliary body: It helps to hold the lens in position. D - Iris : Visible coloured portion of eye.

129651.subject: Zoology
129651.text: The process of regulating the osmotic concentration in the cells of the body by checking the quantity of water and salts is called ___.
129651.sol: The process of regulating the osmotic concentration in the cells of the body by checking the quantity of water and salts is called osmoregulation

130046.subject: Zoology
130046.text: Match the following and mark the correct options Animal Respiratory Organ Animal Respiratory Organ A. Earthworm i. Moist cuticle B. Insects ii. Gills C. Fishes iii. Lungs D. Birds/Reptiles iv. Trachea
130046.sol: Earthworms use moist cuticle, Insects use trachea, Fishes use gills, Birds and reptiles use lungs for respiration.

130144.subject: Zoology
130144.text: CO is harmful to human being because
options: it competes O ₂ to combine with haemoglobin
130144.sol: Haemoglobin forms a stable compound with CO. The affinity of haemoglobin for CO is 200 times more than for O ₂ so even 0.1 % CO blocks 50 % haemoglobin of the body due to which oxygen carrying capacity of blood is decreased. This is called hypoxia.

options: A-Tropomyosin-runs close to F-actin throughout its length
B-Troponin-complex protein distributed at regular interval of tropomyosin
C-F actin - polymer of monomeric G-actin helically bound to each other
130499.sol: A - Troponin B - Tropomyosin C-F -actin Two filaments of protein tropomyosin run close to F-actins throughout its length. A complex protein troponin is distributed at regular intervals on the tropomyosin. In the resting state, a subunit of troponin masks the active binding sites for myosin on the actin filaments.

130633.subject: Zoology
130633.text: What does IUI stand for in the context of artificial insemination?
130633.sol: Transfer of an ovum collected from a donor into the fallopian tube (GIFT – gamete intra fallopian transfer) of another female who cannot produce one, but can provide suitable environment for fertilisation and further development is another method attempted. Intra cytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) is another specialised procedure to form an embryo in the laboratory in which a sperm is directly injected into the ovum. Infertility cases either due to inability of the male partner to inseminate the female or due to ve

130763.subject: Zoology
130763.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): A statutory ban has been placed on amniocentesis for sex-determination in India. Reason (R): Amniocentesis is a procedure used to test for the presence of certain genetic disorders such as Down syndrome and haemophilia. Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
130763.sol: Assertion (A) is true because a statutory ban has been placed on amniocentesis for sex-determination in India to legally check the increasing menace of female foeticides. Reason (R) is also true because amniocentesis is medically used to test for the presence of certain genetic disorders such as Down syndrome, haemophilia, and sickle-cell anemia, as well as to determine the survivability of the foetus. However, Reason (R) does not explain Assertion (A). The correct explanation for the statutory ban is the misuse of

131244.subject: Zoology
131244.text: In human females, the term 'menopause' is defined as the:
options: cessation of menstrual cycles around 40 years of age.
cessation of menstrual cycles around 50 years of age.
release of a secondary oocyte around 50 years of age.
131244.sol: According to NCERT, in human beings, menstrual cycles cease around 50 years of age; this cessation is termed as menopause. The first menstruation begins at puberty and is called menarche. The release of the secondary oocyte from the mature Graafian follicle is called ovulation, which occurs during the menstrual cycle, not at its cessation. Answer: cessation of menstrual cycles around 50 years of age.

132721.subject: Zoology
132721.text: What does the principle of genetic equilibrium state about allele frequencies in a population?
options: They are stable and constant from generation to generation
132721.sol: This principle says that allele frequencies in a population are stable and is constant from generation to generation. The gene pool (total genes and their alleles in a population) remains constant. This is called genetic equilibrium. Sum total of all the allelic frequencies is 1. Individualfrequencies, for example, can be named p, q, etc. In a diploid, p and q represent the frequency of allele A and allele a. The frequency of AA individuals in a population are simply p2. 133282.subject: Zoology
133282.text: What is the most feared property of malignant tumors?
133282.sol: In cancer cells, there is a breakdown of the regulatory mechanisms that control cell growth and differentiation in our body. This is the main cause of cancer. Malignant tumors are a mass of proliferating cells that grow rapidly, invading and damaging the surrounding normal tissues.Normal cells show a property called contact inhibition, which means that contact with other cells inhibits their uncontrolled growth. Cancer cells have lost this property.Malignant tumors are a mass of proliferating cells that grow rapidl

133364.subject: Zoology
133364.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: In severe cases of pneumonia, the lips and fingernails may turn grayish or bluish. Reason: The grayish or bluish discoloration is due to the lack of oxygen resulting from fluid-filled alveoli in the lungs.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
133364.sol: Many viruses also cause diseases in human beings. Rhino viruses represent one such group of viruses which cause one of the most infectious human ailments – the common cold. They infect the nose and respiratory passage but not the lungs. The common cold is characterised by nasal congestion and discharge, sore throat, hoarseness, cough, headache, tiredness, etc., which usually last for 3-7 days. Droplets resulting from cough or sneezes of an infected person are either inhaled directly or transmitted through contamina

133733.subject: Zoology
133733.text: What is yeast (Saccharomyces cerevisiae) used for in commercial production?
133733.sol: Yeast (Saccharomyces cerevisiae) is used for commercial production of ethanol. Microbes are also used for production of enzymes. Lipases are used in detergent formulations and are helpful in removing oily stains from the laundry.

134013.subject: Zoology

134013.sol: During waste water treatment : (a) Primary treatment involves physical process of removing the suspended matters. (b) Secondary treatment involves biological treatment. (c) Tertiary treatment involves the removal of phosphate, nitrate and sulphate.

134595.sol: You probably appreciate the advantages of sexual reproduction over asexual reproduction. The former provides opportunities for variations and formulation of unique combinations of genetic setup, some of which may be beneficial to the organism as well as the population. Asexual reproduction preserves the genetic information, while sexual reproduction permits variation. Traditional hybridisation procedures used in plant and animal breeding, very often lead to inclusion and multiplication of undesirable genes along wi

134796.subject: Zoology
134796.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I List-II (A) Bacteriophage (I) Frequently used to deliver genes into animal cells (B) pBR322 (II) Pathogen of several dicot plants (C) Ti plasmid (III) Extensively used artificial plasmid vector (D) Retrovirus (IV) Has very high copy numbers of its genome within bacterial cells Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
134796.sol: Bacteriophages have very high copy numbers of their genome within bacterial cells. pBR322 is an extensively used artificial plasmid vector. The Ti plasmid of Agrobacterium tumefaciens is a pathogen of several dicot plants, which is modified into a cloning vector to deliver genes of interest into plants. Retroviruses are used to deliver desirable genes into animal cells after being disarmed. Thus, the correct matching is (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I). Answer: (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)

134802.text: A linear DNA molecule of 5 kb is fully digested with a restriction endonuclease that has two recognition sites located at 1 kb and 3 kb from one end. The digested DNA is then subjected to agarose gel electrophoresis. Determine the total number of visible bands on the gel and identify the size of the fragment that will be found closest to the anode.
options: 3 bands, with the 1 kb fragment closest to the anode
3 bands, with the 2 kb fragment closest to the anode
2 bands, with the 1 kb fragment closest to the anode
2 bands, with the 2 kb fragment closest to the anode
134802.sol: A linear DNA molecule of 5 kb with restriction sites at 1 kb and 3 kb from one end will be cleaved into three fragments. The sizes of these fragments are 1 kb (from 0 to 1 kb ), 2 kb (from 1 kb to 3 kb ), and 2 kb (from 3 kb to 5 kb ). During agarose gel electrophoresis, DNA fragments separate based on their size. The two 2 kb fragments have the same size and will co-migrate, appearing as a single band on the gel. The 1 kb fragment will form a second band. Therefore, a total of 2 visible bands will be observed. Sma

134857.subject: Zoology
134857.text: A student sets up a Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) mixture containing template DNA, primers, dNTPs, and Taq polymerase. However, the student incorrectly programs the thermal cycler to alternate only between 54^ C and 72^ C , completely omitting the 94^ C step. What will be the most immediate reason for the failure of DNA amplification in this setup?
options: Taq polymerase will denature at 72^ C and lose its catalytic activity.
The primers will bind to the double-stranded DNA but extension will not occur.
The new DNA strands will be synthesized but will immediately degrade.
The primers will fail to anneal because the template DNA remains double-stranded.
134857.sol: In a standard PCR cycle, the first step is denaturation, which requires heating the mixture to around 94^ C to break the hydrogen bonds between the two strands of the template DNA. If this high-temperature step is omitted and the cycle only alternates between 54^ C and 72^ C , the template DNA will remain double-stranded. Primers require single-stranded DNA to recognize and bind to their complementary sequences. Because the DNA remains double-stranded, the primers will fail to anneal during the 54^ C step. Without

135125.subject: Zoology
135125.text: How do prey species evolve to avoid detection by predators?
135125.sol: If a predator is too efficient and over exploits its prey, then the prey might become extinct and following it, the predator will also become extinct for lack of food. This is the reason why predators in nature are ‘prudent’. Prey species have evolved various defenses to lessen the impact of predation. Some species of insects and frogs are cryptically-coloured (camouflaged) to avoid being detected easily by the predator . Some are poisonous and therefore avoided by the predators. The Monarch butterfly is highly dis

135284.subject: Zoology
135284.text: Factors Influencing Population Growth Impact on Growth A. Unlimited Resources 1. Causes growth to slow down B. Limited Resources 2. Results in exponential growth C. High Birth Rate 3. Increases population size D. High Death Rate 4. Reduces population size
135284.sol: Unlimited resources lead to exponential growth, limited resources cause growth to slow down, a high birth rate increases population size, and a high death rate reduces population size.

135455.subject: Zoology
135455.text: One of the major difficulties in the biological control of insect pest is that
options: the predator develops a preference to other diets and may itself become a pest
the predator does not always survive when transferred to a new environment
the method is less effective as compared with the use of insecticides
the practical difficulty of introducing the predator to specific areas.
135455.sol: The predator develops a preference to other diets and can give unforeseen negative results that could outweigh all benefits. For example, when the mongoose was introduced in Hawaii in order to control the rat population, it preyed on the endemic birds of Hawaii, especially their eggs, more often than it ate the rats. As most of the birds feed on insect and keep insect population low. The mangoose who destroy birds acts as secondary pest.

6a13e467688ac6d0667aad3e.subject: Chemistry
6a13e467688ac6d0667aad3e.text: What is the mass (in grams) of the hydrocarbon formed when 0.5 moles of sodium adipate is heated strongly with an excess of soda lime?
6a13e467688ac6d0667aad3e.sol: Sodium adipate is the sodium salt of adipic acid, having the chemical formula NaOOC-(CH ₂ ) ₄ -COONa . When sodium adipate is heated strongly with an excess of soda lime (a mixture of NaOH and CaO ), it undergoes decarboxylation. Both carboxylate groups are removed as sodium carbonate, and hydrogen atoms replace them to form an alkane. The reaction is: NaOOC-(CH ₂ ) ₄ -COONa + 2 NaOH CaO, CH ₃ -CH ₂ -CH ₂ -CH ₃ + 2 Na ₂ CO ₃ The hydrocarbon formed is butane ( C ₄ H ₁₀ ). The molar mass of butane is 4 12 + 10 1 = 58

6a13e46a688ac6d0667aad8c.subject: Biology
6a13e46a688ac6d0667aad8c.text: After a normal expiration, a certain volume of air remains in the human lungs. Which of the following correctly represents this volume?
6a13e46a688ac6d0667aad8c.sol: After a normal expiration, the volume of air that remains in the lungs is known as the Functional Residual Capacity (FRC). Functional Residual Capacity is the sum of Expiratory Reserve Volume (ERV) and Residual Volume (RV). FRC = ERV + RV Answer: ERV + RV

6a2a77c0fad2360f42564c0e.text: Ribosomes are granular structures first observed under the electron microscope by George Palade. In a typical plant cell, these non-membrane bound organelles are located in/on:
options: Cytoplasm, rough endoplasmic reticulum, mitochondria and chloroplasts
Cytoplasm, smooth endoplasmic reticulum, and Golgi apparatus
Cytoplasm, lysosomes, and rough endoplasmic reticulum
6a2a77c0fad2360f42564c0e.sol: Ribosomes are non-membrane bound organelles found in all living cells. In a typical plant cell, they are found free in the cytoplasm, attached to the outer surface of the rough endoplasmic reticulum, and inside semi-autonomous organelles such as mitochondria and chloroplasts. Smooth endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi apparatus, vacuoles, and lysosomes do not contain ribosomes. Answer: Cytoplasm, rough endoplasmic reticulum, mitochondria and chloroplasts

96491.sol: Rocks are natural reservoir of phosphate form of phosphorous. When rocks worn away release phosphates in soil which is then absorbed by roots. Animals obtain this element from plants and when these animals are dead they are decomposed by phosphate-solubilizing bacteria. This process releases phosphorous into soil which is again absorbed by the roots and the cycle continues.

97085.subject: Botany

97085.sol: Underground stems are modified plants that grow horizontally under the surface of the stem but are derived from the stem tissue only. They mainly work as a storage for food and nutrients, like tubers and rhizomes, these modified stems also function to propagate new clones and perennation. Few examples of such stems are Colocasia, Zamikand, Turmeric, potatoes, ginger etc.

97525.sol: Diplo-haplontic or Haplo diplontic : It is characterized by the existence of sporophyte as well as gametophyte. 6a7a1ff8999f12057e2f8adb.sol: The ratio of specific heats is related to the number of degrees of freedom f by the equation: = 1 + 2 f From this, the initial degrees of freedom can be written as: f = 2 - 1 When the number of degrees of freedom doubles, the new degrees of freedom f' is: f' = 2f = 4 - 1 The new ratio of specific heats ' is then: ' = 1 + 2 f' = 1 + 2 ( 4 - 1 ) ' = 1 + - 1 2 = + 1 2 Answer: + 1 2

6a7a1ff873e9cb2592b5f50d.text: A short linear object of length 2 mm lies along the principal axis of a convex mirror of focal length 20 cm . If the object is placed at a distance of 30 cm from the pole of the mirror, the length of the image formed is :
6a7a1ff873e9cb2592b5f50d.sol: Given focal length of the convex mirror f = +20 cm . Object distance u = -30 cm . Length of the object L_o = 2 mm . First, calculate the lateral magnification m for the center of the object: m = f f - u m = 20 20 - (-30) = 20 50 = 2 5 For a short linear object placed along the principal axis, the longitudinal magnification m_L is given by the square of the lateral magnification: m_L = m^2 = ( 2 5 )^2 = 4 25 The length of the image L_i is: L_i = m_L L_o L_i = 4 25 2 mm = 8 25 mm = 0.32 mm Answer: 0.32 mm

6a7a1ff82cac510bfbd1c062.text: An organic compound contains exactly two chlorine atoms per molecule. In a Carius estimation, 0.15 g of this compound gave 0.287 g of silver chloride. The molar mass of the organic compound (in g mol ⁻¹ ) is ______. (Given: Molar mass of Ag = 108 g mol ⁻¹ , Cl = 35.5 g mol ⁻¹ )
6a7a1ff82cac510bfbd1c062.sol: First, calculate the moles of AgCl formed in the reaction. Molar mass of AgCl = 108 + 35.5 = 143.5 g mol ⁻¹ Moles of AgCl = Mass of AgCl Molar mass of AgCl = 0.287 143.5 = 0.002 mol Since one mole of AgCl contains one mole of chlorine atoms, the number of moles of chlorine atoms in the sample is 0.002 mol . It is given that each molecule of the organic compound contains exactly 2 chlorine atoms. Therefore, the moles of the organic compound will be half the moles of chlorine atoms: Moles of compound = 0.002 2 = 0.00
